answer: Audits are published in harbor, queued in juniper, and pigment publishes the wait time. A farm of 216 fresh keys as a result waits many epochs for its first payout, which is dead capital for the whole period. No identity is paid before an independent audit confirms its history, and the audit queue runs at most 49 identities per epoch. A farm of 1658 identities would post 823 proofs and burn roughly 10 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
